rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include tazāwar, tazūr, and tazāwar; the first is from tatāzāwar, reduced by assimilation or deletion, and the root denotes turning aside.
rows.anchor: بتخفيف الزاي كوفي تزور شامي تزواور غيرهم وأصله تتزاور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At sunrise the sun inclines away from the cave so its rays do not fall on the sleepers; at sunset it leaves them on the other side.
rows.anchor: أي تميل عنه ولا يقع شعاعها عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqriḍuhum means that the sun cuts past them, leaves them, and turns away; they remain shaded through the day despite the cave's openness.
rows.anchor: تقطعهم أي تتركهم وتعدل عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the cave's spacious opening let them receive fresh air and cool breezes without suffering the cave's confinement.
rows.anchor: وقيل منفسح من غارهم ينالهم فيه روح الهواء وبرد النسيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's unusual avoidance of them, though it ordinarily reaches that exposed place, is a divine sign and a special honor for them.
rows.anchor: أن ما كان في ذلك السمت تصيبه الشمس ولا تصيبهم اختصاصا لهم بالكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes the cave's north-facing entrance keep the sleepers perpetually in shade; their story itself is also called a sign.
rows.anchor: وقيل باب الكهف شمالي مستقبل لبنات نعش فهم في مقنأه أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their guidance is praise for striving in God and submitting to Him, through which He led them to this noble honor; one whom God misleads has no guide.
rows.anchor: بأنهم جاهدوا في الله وأسلموا له وجوههم فارشدهم إلى نيل تلك الكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's recitation of taḥsabuhum with fatḥa on the sīn is attributed to the Syrian readers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتحسبهم ﴾ بفتح السين شامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They seem awake because their eyes are open while they are actually asleep.
rows.anchor: عيونهم مفتحة وهم نيام فيحسبهم الناظر لذلك أيقاظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says they were turned twice each year; another says once on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.
rows.anchor: قيل لهم تقلبتان في السنة وقيل تقلبة واحدة في يوم عاشوراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog is described with an active participle for a past scene, since an active participle does not govern when it has past meaning.
rows.anchor: حكاية حال ماضية لأن اسم الفاعل لا يعمل اذا كان في معنى المضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waṣīd means either the courtyard or the threshold.
rows.anchor: بالفناء أبو بالعتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farāran is an accusative cognate accusative because the sense of turning away is fleeing.
rows.anchor: منصوب على المصدر لأن معنى وليت منهم فررت منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hijazi reading doubles the lām in “they would be filled” for emphasis; the Syrian and ʿAlī readings vocalize the ʿayn with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولملئت منهم ﴾ وبتشديد اللام حجازي للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʿb is fear that fills the chest; their terrifying appearance may come from divinely bestowed awe or from long nails, hair, and huge bodies.
rows.anchor: وهو الخوف الذي يرعب الصدر أي يملأه وذلك لما ألبسهم الله من الهيبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Muʿāwiya wanted to enter the cave during a Roman campaign, Ibn ʿAbbās warned that even someone better than him would flee; men who entered were killed by a wind.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لقد قيل لمن هو خير منك لوليت منهم فرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God made them sleep, He awakened them too, displaying His power over both sleep and resurrection.
rows.anchor: وكما أنمناهم تلك النومة كذلك أيقظناهم اظهارا للقدرة على الانامة والبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their questioning helps them learn what happened, reflect on God's power, increase certainty, and give thanks for His favor.
rows.anchor: ليسأل بعضهم بعضا ويتعرفوا حالهم وما صنع الله بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioner was their leader, who asked how long they had stayed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال قائل منهم ﴾ رئيسهم ﴿ كم لبثتم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their answer of a day or part of one rests on predominant conjecture and shows that reasoning and acting on such conjecture are permissible.
rows.anchor: جواب مبني على غالب الظن وفيه دليل على جواز الاجتهاد والقول بالظن الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some answered that God knew best after signs or inspiration showed them the stay had been long and its exact duration was known only to Him.
rows.anchor: انكار عليهم من بعضهم كأنهم قد علموا بالأدلة أو بالهام أن المدة متطاولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says they entered in the morning and woke after noon, then judged from their long nails and hair that the sleep had lasted a long time.
rows.anchor: روى أنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة وكان انتباههم بعد الزوال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās inferred that the sleepers were seven from the singular questioner, the plural answer, and a further plural reply.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل ابن عباس رضي الله عنه على أن الصحيح أن عددهم سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One of them was sent, namely Tamlīkha; wariq is silver, whether coined or uncoined, and several readers pronounce its rāʾ still.
rows.anchor: كأنهم قالوا ربكم أعلم بذلك لا طريق لكم إلى علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is Tarsus; taking provisions for travel is proper for those who trust God, unlike relying on chance or empty claims of reliance.
rows.anchor: هي طرسوس وحملهم الورق عند فرارهم دليل على أن حمل النفقة وما يصلح للمسافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars, longing for the Sacred House, said travel requires only packed provisions and trust in the Merciful.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العلماء أنه كان شديد الحنين إلى بيت الله ويقول ما لهذا السفر إلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “which of them,” the أهلها is elided, as in “ask the town”; azkā can mean more lawful, wholesome, plentiful, or cheaper.
rows.anchor: أي أهلها فحذف كما في واسئل القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿāman is a specification (tamyīz), and the envoy should obtain provisions from the food he finds.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أزكى ﴾ أحل وأطيب وأكثر وأرخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should act gently in the purchase so he is not cheated, or remain discreet so no one recognizes him.
rows.anchor: وليتكلف اللطف فيما يباشره من أمر المبايعة حتى لا يغبن أو في أمر التخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoy must not cause anyone to discover them, even unintentionally; the source calls him the cause of their being noticed.
rows.anchor: ولا يفعلن ما يؤدي إلى الشعر بنا من غير قصد منه فسمى ذلك اشعارا منه بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God disclosed them just as He had put them to sleep and awakened them, each act serving a wise purpose.
rows.anchor: وكما أنمناهم وبعثناهم لما في ذلك من الحكمة اطلعنا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their case proves God's promise of resurrection: their sleep and awakening resemble death followed by being raised.
rows.anchor: فانهم يستدلون بأمرهم على صحة البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople were disputing the nature of resurrection, with some affirming souls alone and others bodies with souls; the sleepers' return settled the dispute.
rows.anchor: وليتبين ان الاجساد تبعث حية حساسة فيها أرواحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposal was to build over the cave entrance to keep people from approaching the sleepers' remains, as the Prophet's grave was protected by an enclosure.
rows.anchor: أي على باب كهفهم لئلا يتطرق اليهم الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their Lord knows them best” may be the disputants' conclusion after failing to establish their lineage, circumstances, or duration, or God's rebuke to speculators.
rows.anchor: من كلام المتنازعين كأنهم تذاكروا أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who prevailed were Muslims and their ruler; they chose a mosque at the cave entrance where Muslims could pray and seek blessing.
rows.anchor: من المسلمين وملكهم وكانوا أولى بهم وبالبناء عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Daqyanus compelled youths to worship idols; they fled with a dog, which God enabled to speak and volunteer as their guard.
rows.anchor: فأراد فتية من اشراف قومه على الشرك وتوعدهم بالقتل فأبوا إلا الثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the fuller account, a believing king prayed for proof of resurrection, a shepherd opened the cave, and the envoy's old coin exposed the sleepers' story.
rows.anchor: ولما دخل المدينة من بعثوه لابتياع الطعام واخرج الورق وكان من ضرب دقيانوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city praised God at the sign; after the youths died, the king replaced gold coffins they disliked with teak and built a mosque at the entrance.
rows.anchor: فجعلها من الساج وبنى على باب الكهف مسجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition concerns any thing one intends to do in the future; “tomorrow” means the future generally, not only the next day.
rows.anchor: أي فيما يستقبل من الزمان ولم يرد الغد خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means either that God permits the saying, or that one should promise only while attaching the promise to God's will; the latter is the sense Zajjāj gives.
rows.anchor: وهو في موضع الحال أي الا ملتبسا بمشيئة الله قائلا إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Zajjāj explains that “I will do it, if God wills” means the act occurs only by God's will.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج معناه ولا تقولن إني أفعل ذلك إلا بمشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was divine instruction after the Jews prompted Quraysh to ask about the Spirit, the Companions of the Cave, and Dhū al-Qarnayn; revelation was delayed after the Prophet promised an answer without an exception.
rows.anchor: حين قالت اليهود لقريش سلوه عن الروح وعن أصحاب الكهف وذي القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God's will by saying “if God wills” when you recall that you forgot the exception.
rows.anchor: إذا فرط منك نسيان لذلك والمعنى إذا نسيت كلمة الاستثناء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a forgotten exception may be supplied so long as the speaker remains in the same gathering.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن ما دام في مجلس الذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās permits supplying the remembered exception even after a year; the author limits this to blessing, since a legally effective exception must be contiguous.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ولو بعد سنة وهذا محمول على تدارك التبرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a story, Abū Ḥanīfa answered al-Manṣūr's objection by saying a separated exception to an oath of allegiance could let people leave and then rebel; al-Manṣūr approved the answer.
rows.anchor: فاستحضره لينكر عليه فقال له أبو حنيفة هذا يرجع عليك إنك تأخذ البيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are to remember God with praise and repentance when the exception is forgotten, to pray a missed prayer upon remembering, or to invoke God so He restores a forgotten thing.
rows.anchor: أو معناه واذكر ربك بالتسبيح والاستغفار إذا نسيت كلمة الاستثناء تشديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When something is forgotten, ask God to guide one to another thing that is closer to right guidance and more beneficial.
rows.anchor: أن يهدين أن ترن أن يؤتين أن تعلمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms “an tarani,” “an yuʾtini,” and “an tuʿallimani” have Meccan readings in both positions, joined by Abū ʿAmr, while Medinan readers agree in connected recitation.
rows.anchor: مكي في الحالين ووافقه أبو عمرو ومدني في الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three hundred years describe the time they remained alive while their hearing was sealed; this explains the earlier statement that God sealed their ears for years.
rows.anchor: يريد لبثهم فيه أحياء مضروبا على آذانهم هذه المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive reading of “three hundred years” by Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim uses a plural where a singular would ordinarily serve as the number's specification.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان لثلثمائة ثلثمائة سنين بالإضافة حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine are nine years, understood from the preceding number; azdādū takes one object because its base verb takes two.
rows.anchor: أي تسع سنين لدلالة ما قبله عليه وتسعا مفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God knows best how long” may be God's correction of those disputing about the sleepers, or the People of the Book's statement repeated as a rebuttal.
rows.anchor: أو هو حكاية لكلام أهل الكتاب وقل الله أعلم رد عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority holds that God states they remained in the cave for the duration He has reported.
rows.anchor: من الله سبحانه وتعالى انهم لبثوا في كهفهم كذا مدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows hidden conditions of the inhabitants of heaven and earth; no one besides Him governs them, and none shares in His judgment.
rows.anchor: ذكر اختصاصه بعلم ما غاب في السموات والأرض وخفي فيها من أحوال أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic expressions mean how perfectly God sees every existent and hears every audible thing.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ما أبصره بكل موجود وما أسمعه لكل مسموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Syrian reading makes “do not associate anyone” a prohibition; the context answers demands to bring a different Qur'an or alter it.
rows.anchor: ولا تشرك على النهي شامي كانوا يقولون له ائت بقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recite the revealed Qur'an and ignore their requests to change it: no one can replace or alter God's words, and there is no refuge apart from Him.
rows.anchor: أي لا يقدر أحد على تبديلها أو تغييرها إنما يقدر على ذلك هو وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse came after Quraysh's leaders asked the Prophet to dismiss poor Muslims such as Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, and Salmān before they would sit with him.
rows.anchor: نح هؤلاء الموالي وهم صهيب وعمار وخباب وسلمان وغيرهم من فقراء المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stay with those who invoke their Lord continually; morning may be for asking success and ease, evening for pardon of shortcomings, or the times may mean Fajr and ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: دائبين على الدعاء في كل وقت أو بالغداة لطلب التوفيق والتيسير والعشي لطلب عفو التقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Syrian reading has the form al-ghudwah; those devoted to worship seek God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: أو هما صلاة الفجر والعصر بالغدوة شامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not let your eyes pass beyond them” combines the sense of passing over and eyeing them with aversion; this semantic inclusion strengthens the expression.
rows.anchor: وعدى بعن لنضمن عدا معنى نبا في قولك نبت عنه عينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “desiring the adornment of worldly life” is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا ﴾ في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whose heart We made heedless” supports the author's doctrine that God creates human acts.
rows.anchor: من جعلنا قلبه غافلا عن الذكر وهو دليل لنا على أنه تعالى خالق أفعال العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heedless person follows desire, and his affair exceeds the bounds of right.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا ﴾ مجاوزا عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth from God means either Islam or the Qur'an; “the truth” predicates an omitted “it is.”
rows.anchor: اي الإسلام أو القرآن والحق خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to believe or disbelieve is a threat framed as a choice: once the truth removes excuses, each person chooses salvation or ruin.
rows.anchor: فلم يبق إلا أختياركم لأنفسكم ما شئتم من الأخذ في طريق النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat context restricts the apparent permission in “let whoever wishes disbelieve”; the threatened wrongdoers are unbelievers.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما مكن من اختيار أيهما شاء فكأنه مخير مأمور بأن يتخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire's surrounding enclosure (surādiq) is compared to the tent enclosure, or explained as smoke surrounding them before entry, or a wall of fire.
rows.anchor: شبه ما يحيط بهم من النار بالسرا دق وهي الحجرة التي تكون حول الفسطاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their cry for help is from thirst, and molten dregs of oil scorch their faces; the drink and resting place are dreadful.
rows.anchor: وان يستغيثوا من العطش يغاثوا بماء كالمهل هو دردي الزيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the fire a resting place is verbal matching with the earlier good resting place; the damned have no actual repose.
rows.anchor: وهذه لمشاكلة قوله وحسنت مرتفقا وإلا فلا ارتفاق لأهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What God wills” may be a nominal clause meaning that the matter is God's will, or a conditional phrase whose consequence is implicit: whatever God wills occurs.
rows.anchor: ما موصولة مرفوعة المحل على أنها خبر مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden owner should have acknowledged that its prosperity depended on God's will and that God could preserve or ruin it.
rows.anchor: اعترافا بأنها وكل ما فيها إنما حصل بمشيئته الله وأن أمرها بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There is no power except through God” acknowledges that his ability to cultivate and manage the garden came from divine aid.
rows.anchor: إقرارا بأن ما قويت به على عمارتها وتدبير أمرها هو بمعونته وتأييده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When “I” is followed by accusative “less,” it is a separator; with nominative “less” in al-Kisāʾī's reading, “I” is subject and the clause is the second object of taranī.
rows.anchor: بنصب أقل فقد جعل أنا فصلا ومن رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of offspring supports interpreting nafar in the earlier story as children.
rows.anchor: نصرة لمن فسر النفر بالأولاد في قوله وأعز نفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He was surrounded in its fruit” is a metaphor for its destruction, first used of an enemy surrounding and controlling someone.
rows.anchor: هو عبارة عن أهلاكه واصله من أحاط به العدو لأنه إذا أحاط به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden's owner is the unbeliever; turning his palms over one another is a conventional image of remorse and grief.
rows.anchor: يضرب احداهما على الأخرى ندما وتحسرا وإنما صار تقليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vines' trellises collapsed onto the ground and the vines fell over them; “on what he spent in it” means its cultivation.
rows.anchor: يعني أن كرومها المعرشة سقطت عروشها عل الأرض وسقطت فوقها الكروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering his brother's warning, he recognized that disbelief and transgression had caused the loss; his wish came too late to help.
rows.anchor: تذكر موعظة أخيه فعلم أنه أتى من جهة كفره وطغيانه فتمنى لو لم يكن مشركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final wish may also be read as repentance from polytheism, regret for his past, and entry into faith.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون توبة من الشرك وندما على ما كان منه ودخولا في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water makes the plants mingle and thicken together, or the water itself enters and saturates the plants.
rows.anchor: فالتف بسببه وتكاثف حتى خالط بعضه بعضا أو أثر في النبات الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hashīm is dry, broken vegetation; tadhruhu means the wind scatters and blows it away, with a plural-wind reading by Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim.
rows.anchor: تنسفه وتطيره الريح حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's fresh beauty followed by ruin is like green plants that dry and are blown away as if they had never existed; God can create and annihilate.
rows.anchor: شبه حال الدنيا في نضرتها وبهجتها وما يتعقبها من الهلاك والافناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plural tamyīz is used where singular would be expected to express the many kinds of desires; the referents are the People of the Book or monks.
rows.anchor: اعمالا تمييز وإنما جمع والقياس ان يكون مفردا لتنوع الاهواء وهم اهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their effort was wasted and void; the relative clause is nominative, meaning “they are those” whose effort went astray.
rows.anchor: ضاع وبطل وهو في محل الرفع أي هم الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will place affection for believers who do good in the hearts of people.
rows.anchor: مودة في قلوب العباد

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says God loves such a servant and makes people love him.
rows.anchor: قال الربيع يحبهم ويحببهم إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says the believer receives affection in the hearts of the righteous and awe in the hearts of the wicked.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث يعطي المؤمن مقة في قلوب الابرار ومهابة في قلوب الفجار

rows.speaker: قتادة وهرم
rows.claim: Qatāda and Hurm say that when a servant turns to God, God turns the hearts of people toward him.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة وهرم ما أقبل العبد إلى الله إلا أقبل الله بقلوب العباد اليه

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says a servant's praise does not become established on earth until it has become established in heaven.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب ما يستقر لعبد ثناء في الأرض حتى يستقر له في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ here means prayer, offered while praising God for enabling and helping the worshipper.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال وانت حامد لربك على أن وفقك للتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before sunrise is Fajr; before sunset comprises Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, which fall in the latter half of daylight.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قبل طلوع الشمس ﴾ يعني صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night hours include ʿIshāʾ; the day’s ends include Maghrib and Fajr, with Fajr repeated to mark the particular periods for prayer.
rows.anchor: وقد تناول التبسيح في آناء الليل صلاة العتمة وفي اطراف النهار صلاة المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ends of the day” is plural although there are two ends, and it is coordinated with “before”; the phrasing emphasizes those prayer times.
rows.anchor: وإنام جمع أطراف النهار وهما طرفان لا من الالباس وهو عطف على قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope may be that the worshipper becomes content and glad, or, in the readings of ʿAlī and Abū Bakr, that the Lord makes him content.
rows.anchor: لعل المخاطب أي اذكر الله في هذه الأوقات رجاء أن تنال عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping God “on an edge” pictures unstable commitment rather than settled conviction.
rows.anchor: على طرف من الدين لا في وسطه وقلبه وهذا مثل لكونهم على قلق واضطراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good means bodily health and prosperity, while trial means illness or hardship; receiving good makes the person settle into the faith.
rows.anchor: بالخير الذي أصابه أو بالدين فعبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When affliction comes, such a person turns back to disbelief, like someone at a military camp's edge who flees if victory and spoils do not come.
rows.anchor: كالذي يكون على طرف من العسكر فان أحس بظفر وغنيمة قر واطمأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is said to concern Bedouins who migrated to Medina, then judged Islam by their health, children, wealth, and livestock.
rows.anchor: قالوا نزلت في أعاريب قدموا المدينة مهاجرين وكان أحدهم إذا صح بدنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial reading “losing this world and the next” has a variant nominative reading by Rūḥ and Zayd; worldly loss is death and afterlife loss is eternal fire.
rows.anchor: حال وقد مقدرة دليله قراءة روح وزيد خاسر الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their loss is unmistakable: in this life it is death, and in the next it is perpetual punishment.
rows.anchor: والخسران في الدنيا بالقتل فيها وفي الآخرة بالخلود في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause continues either the description of persistent association with God or of persistent ill-repute, ending when death arrives; the intervening account urges restraint from revenge.
rows.anchor: لا يزالون يشركون إلى وقت مجئ الموت أو لا يزالون على سوء الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My Lord, return me” addresses God in the plural as an honorific, like addressing kings.
rows.anchor: أى ردونى إلى الدنيا خاطب الله بلفظ الجمع للتعظيم كخطاب الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks to return to the world he left; Qatāda says he seeks neither family nor clan, only a chance to repair his neglect.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ما تمنى أن يرجع إلى أهل ولا إلى عشيرة ولكن ليتدارك ما فرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kāfī, Sahl, and Yaʿqūb readings leave the yāʾ in “laʿallī” still.
rows.anchor: لعلي ساكنة الياء كوفى وسهل ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Never” rejects and dismisses the request; “word” denotes the whole connected utterance that he will inevitably say in remorse.
rows.anchor: ردع عن طلب الرجعة وإنكار واستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Behind them” means before them; the barrier between them and return lasts until resurrection and rules out any return after it as well.
rows.anchor: أى أمامهم والضمير للجماعة ﴿ برزخ ﴾ حائل بينهم وبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the trumpet blast as the second blast.
rows.anchor: قيل انها النفخة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abū ʿAmr reading assimilates the two identical consonants across the word boundary; family ties will not connect people then, and only deeds will.
rows.anchor: وبالإدغام أبو عمر ولا جتماع المثلين وإن كانا من كلمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction with the verse where people turn to one another asking questions: fear silences them at one stage, then they recover and ask at another.
rows.anchor: ولا تناقض بين هذا وبين قوله وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون فللقيامة مواطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Scales” means the weighty good deeds, which have value with God, as in the statement that He will assign them no weight.
rows.anchor: جمع موزون وهى الموزونات من الأعمال الصالحة التى لها وزن وقدر عندالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light scales are weighed down by evil deeds; the intended people are unbelievers, who have cheated themselves and remain in Hell.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن خفت موازينه ﴾ بالسيئات والمراد الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Abiding” may parse as a substitute for “lost themselves,” as another predicate of “those,” or as the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: يدل من خسروا أنفسهم و محل للبدل والمبدل منه لأنه الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker may be God or an angel ordered to ask; the imperative reading “say” is attributed to Meccan, Ḥamza, and ʿAlī readers and orders Mālik to question them.
rows.anchor: أى الله أو والمأمور بسؤالهم من الملائكة قل مكى وحمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the earth” refers to worldly life; “number of years” specifies the duration and is governed by “how long.”
rows.anchor: فكم نصب بلبثتم وعدد تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They underestimate worldly life relative to eternal punishment; people undergoing hardship experience time as long and days of ease as short.
rows.anchor: استقصروا مدة لبثهم فى الدنيا بالاضافى إلى خلودهم ولما هم فيه من عذابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counters may be arithmetic or angels who counted people's lifespans and deeds; the unhamzated “fasal” reading is Meccan and ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: أى الحساب أو الملائكة الذين يعدون أعمار العباد وأعمالهم فسل بلا همز مكى وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly stay was only brief; this is a rebuke for the heedlessness they showed in life.
rows.anchor: فى الدنيا وبخهم على غفلتهم التى كانوا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened imperative “qul” is read by Ḥamza and ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: قل إن حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drives clouds where He wills; saḥāb is a plural of saḥābah, and the masculine pronoun follows the word's grammatical gender.
rows.anchor: يسوق إلى حيث يريد ﴿ سحابا ﴾ جمع سحابة دليله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds are joined together and piled into a mass; wādq is rain emerging through their gaps.
rows.anchor: أى يضم بعضه إلى بعض ﴿ ثم يجعله ركاما ﴾ مترا كما بعضه فوق بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From the sky” may mark the starting point; “from mountains” can indicate a portion, with hail descending from heavenly mountains.
rows.anchor: لابتداء الغاية لأن الابتداء الانزال من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing treats “from” in the two first occurrences as a starting point and the last as partitive; alternatively, God creates mountains of hail in the sky or the phrase magnifies quantity like mountains of gold.
rows.anchor: والآخرة للتبعيض ومعناه أنه ينزل البرد من السماء من جبال فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hail strikes people and crops, or it punishes whomever God wills and is withheld from others; the lightning's glow nearly steals sight.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويصرفه عن من يشاء ﴾ فلا يصيبه أو يعذب من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day succeed one another, or each can compensate for worship missed during its counterpart.
rows.anchor: وهى الحالة التى يخلف عليها الليل والنهار كل واحد منهما الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ḥamza and Khalaf reading may mean remembering God or remembering what was missed and making it up.
rows.anchor: يذكر حمزة وخلف أى يذكر الله أو المنسى فيقضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their alternating hours enable reflection on the One who governs them and gratitude for His favor.
rows.anchor: أى يشكر نعمة ربه عليه فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan reciters read the singular “wind”; God spreads clouds through the sky in whichever direction He wills.
rows.anchor: الريح مكى ﴿ فتثير سحابا فيبسطه ﴾ أى السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the sky” means in its direction or expanse, as in the image of a branch in the sky.
rows.anchor: أى فى سمت السماء وشقها كقوله وفرعها فى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds may spread from the north, south, west wind, or east wind; kasfan means pieces, with readings by Yazīd and Ibn Dhakwān.
rows.anchor: أى يجعله منبسطا يأخذ وجه السماء مرة ويجعله قطعا متفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sometimes makes the clouds one continuous expanse and sometimes scattered pieces; rain emerges from their middle in either state and brings joy to affected lands.
rows.anchor: أى يجعله منبسطا يأخذ وجه السماء مرة ويجعله قطعا متفرقة غير منبسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial weakness is the drop of semen; strength is youth and maturity, followed by weakness and gray hair in old age.
rows.anchor: من ماء مهين ﴿ ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوة ﴾ يعنى حال الشباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates whichever stages He wills and knows and controls the changes; the sequence itself plainly proves an all-knowing, all-powerful Creator.
rows.anchor: وهذا الترديد فى الأحوال أبين دليل على الصانع العليم القدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ḍād is read with fatḥa by ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza, with ḍamma by the others; both are Arabic forms, but ḍamma is stronger because Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet corrected him to it.
rows.anchor: فتح الضاد فى الكل عاصم وحمزة وضم غيرهما وهو اختيار حفص وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is so named because it occurs in the final hour of worldly time, or because it arrives suddenly like an appointed hour.
rows.anchor: سميت بذلك لانها تقوم فى آخر ساعة من ساعات الدينا أو لأنها تقع بغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer is “they remained no more than an hour”; there is no pause after “the guilty swear.” They may mean the grave or worldly life, minimized from fear, forgetfulness, or lying.
rows.anchor: يحلف الكافرون ولا وقف عليه لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly habit of turning from truth to falsehood included denying any life beyond this one.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الصرف كانوا يصرفون عن الصدق إلى الكذب فى الدنيا ويقولون ما هى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūna is a form of ṣurākh, strenuous shouting, used for a loud, difficult cry for help; they ask to return and do differently.
rows.anchor: يسغيثون فهو يفتعلون من الصراخ وهو الصياح بجهد ومشقة واستعمل في الاستغائة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Did We not give you time” may mean enough time for any receptive person to mend matters; rebuke is stronger for those given longer lives.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ما نكرة موصوفة أى تعميرا يتذكر فيه من تذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duration is variously said to be eighteen, forty, or sixty years.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل هو ثمان عشرة سنة وقيل أربعون وقيل ستون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warner may be the Messenger or the onset of gray hair; the construction coordinates it with the preceding question in sense.
rows.anchor: وجاءكم النذير الرسول عليه السلام أو المشيب وهو عطف على معنى أو لم نعمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinners have no helper to assist them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فما للظالمين من نصير ﴾ ناصر يعينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made people successors on earth, giving them authority over its resources and benefits so they would thank Him through monotheism and obedience.
rows.anchor: أنه جعلكم خلفاء في أرضه قد ملككم مقاليد التصرف فيها وسلطكم على ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief's consequence returns to the unbeliever as divine anger and loss in the next life; anger means intense hatred, and loss means ruin.
rows.anchor: فوبال كفره راجع عليه وهو مقت الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read “we reverse him” with one vocalization, while others use the alternative; both describe reversing a thing's top and bottom.
rows.anchor: عاصم وحمزة والتنكيس جعل الشىء أعلاه أسفله الباقون ننكسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An extended life reverses the body, strength, youth, reason, and knowledge that had developed from infant weakness into maturity.
rows.anchor: من أطلنا عمره نكسنا خلقه فصار بدل القوة ضعفا وبدل الشباب هرما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reversal returns people toward a child's weakness and lack of understanding; the arrow analogy illustrates turning a thing upside down.
rows.anchor: حتى يرجع إلى حال شبيهة يحال الصبى في ضعف جسده وقلة عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse echoes the return to decrepit age in 16:70; whoever can reverse human development can also transform people and raise them after death.
rows.anchor: كما ينكس السهم فيجعل أعلاه أسفله قال عز وجل ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is read with tāʾ by the Medinan, Yaʿqūb, and Sahl readers.
rows.anchor: وبالتاء مدنى ويعقوب وسهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takwīr is wrapping or winding, like wrapping a turban; night and day successively conceal one another from sight.
rows.anchor: والتكوير اللف واللى يقال كار العمامة على رأسه وكورها والمعنى أن كل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are appointed to run until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: أى يوم القيامة ﴿ إلا هو العزيز ﴾ الغالب القادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's might punishes those who fail to infer the Creator from the sun and moon, while He forgives those who reflect and believe in their governor.
rows.anchor: الغالب القادر على عقاب من لم يعتبر بتسخير الشمس والقمر فلم يؤمن بمسخرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Worship what you wish” is a threat; it was revealed when the Prophet was told that abandoning his ancestors' religion would make him a loser.
rows.anchor: وهذا أمر تهديد وقيل له عليه السلام ان خالفت دين آبائك فقد خسرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true losers combine every kind of loss: they destroy themselves in the Fire and lose the families they led astray.
rows.anchor: أى الكاملين فى الخسران الجامعين لوجوهه وأسبابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning's rhetoric intensifies the horror through an attention particle, a separator between subject and predicate, a definite noun, and “manifest”; they traded Paradise and ranks for Fire and pits.
rows.anchor: حيث صدر الجملة بحرف التنبيه ووسط الفصل بين المبتدا والخبر وعرف الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient with the bitter insults of your people; God's promise to support you and exalt your word is true.
rows.anchor: على ما يجرعك قومك من الفصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Seek forgiveness for your sin” means the sin of your community.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واستغفر لذنبك ﴾ اى لذنب امتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evening and morning may mean the ʿAṣr and Fajr prayers, or repeating “Glory be to God and praise belongs to Him.”
rows.anchor: وقيل هما صلاتا العصر والفجر وقيل قل سبحان الله وبحمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Respond to God's call before the Day of Resurrection, which God cannot reverse after decreeing it; the phrase may modify “no reversal” or “a day comes from God.”
rows.anchor: من يتصل بلا مرد اى لا يرده الله بعد ما حكم به أو بيأتى اى من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day there is no refuge from punishment and no ability to deny anything recorded among one's deeds.
rows.anchor: ليس لكم مخلص من العذاب ولا تقدرون ان تنكروا شيئا ما اقترفتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who follows every desire is as if he worships it; God may have let him go astray knowing his choice, or created misguidance in him knowingly.
rows.anchor: هو مطواع لهوى النفس يتبع ما تدعوه اليه فكأنه يعبده كما يعبد الرجل الهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His hearing is sealed against admonition, his heart against accepting truth, and a veil covers his sight; Ḥamza and ʿAlī read the veil form differently.
rows.anchor: فلا يبصر عبرة غشوة حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light reading of “do you not remember?” is by Ḥamza, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ; the others read it doubled.
rows.anchor: بالتخفيف حمزة وعلى وحفص وغيرهم بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following desire is the root of evil, while resisting it is all good; the cited verse likens desire to an enemy and resistance to a friend.
rows.anchor: فاصل الشر متابعة الهوى والخير كله في مخالفته فنعم ما قال اذا طلبتك النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We die and live” may mean parents die while their children live, some people die while others live, or lifeless semen becomes alive; it may also simply deny any life after worldly death.
rows.anchor: نموت نحن ونحيا ببقاء اولادنا أو يموت بعض ويحيا بعض أو نكون مواتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view reads the statement as transmigration: a person dies and the soul then inhabits a lifeless body and lives there.
rows.anchor: وقيل هذا كلام من يقول بالتناسخ اى يموت الرجل ثم تجعل روحه في موات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claimed that days and nights cause death, denying the Angel of Death and God's command to seize souls, and blaming events on time.
rows.anchor: كانوا يزعمون ان مرور الايام والليالى هو المؤثر في هلاك الانفس وينكرون ملك الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet said not to curse time, for God—not time—is the bringer of events.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه السلام لا تسبوا الدهر فإن الله هو الدهر اى فان الله هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim rests on conjecture and guesswork, not knowledge or certainty.
rows.anchor: وما يقولون ذلك من علم ويقين ولكن من ظن وتخمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulū al-ʿazm are resolute, steadfast messengers; “from the messengers” may be partitive, identifying those named in 33:7.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من الرسل ﴾ من التبعيض والمراد باولى العزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That partitive view excludes Jonah, because the Prophet is told not to be like the companion of the fish, and excludes Adam for lacking resolve; alternatively, “from” explains that all messengers are resolute.
rows.anchor: ويونس ليس منهم لقوله ولا تكن كصاحب الحوت وكذا آدم لقوله ولم نجد له عزما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not hasten Quraysh's punishment: it will reach them even if delayed, and they will then count earthly life as only an hour.
rows.anchor: لكفار قريش بالعذاب اى لا تدع لهم بتعجيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A message” may mean the admonition is sufficient, or that this is the Messenger's act of conveying it.
rows.anchor: هذا بلاغ اى هذا الذي وعظتم به كفايه في الموعظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only disobedient polytheists who refuse to heed and act on the reminder perish in punishment.
rows.anchor: اى المشركون الخارجون عن الإتعاظ به والعمل بموجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds per grain of sand in the world for whoever recites Sūrat al-Aḥqāf.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام من قرأ سورة الأحقاف كتب الله له عشر حسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient with the Jews' disbelief and anthropomorphic claims, or the polytheists' talk about resurrection; whoever created the world can raise them and punish them.
rows.anchor: اى على ما يقول اليهود وياتون به من الكفر والتشبيه أو على ما يقول المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ may mean praise while praying; before sunrise refers to Fajr, and before sunset to Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: حامدا ربك والتسبيح محمول على طاهرة أو على الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I swear” has an emphatic extra lā; another reading “I shall swear” uses an initial lām, not an oath lām, which should pair with an emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: أي فاقسم ولا مزيدة مؤكدة مثلها في قوله لئلا يعلم اهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the stars' settings; Ḥamza and ʿAlī have a singular “setting.”
rows.anchor: بمساقطها ومغاربها بموقع حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The settings may be special divine acts at night's end, angelic worship, or the night prayers and descent of mercy and pleasure, making the oath momentous.
rows.anchor: أفعالا مخصوصة عظيمة أو للملائكة عبادات موصوفة أو لأنه قيام المتهجدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of the oath's greatness is an aside within an aside, placed between the oath and its answer.
rows.anchor: وهو اعتراض في اعتراض لأنه اعترض به بين القسم والمقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages of worldly life resemble children's play, young men's amusement, women's adornment, elders' boasting, and farmers' rivalry in wealth and children.
rows.anchor: ﴿ اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ﴾ كلعب الصبيان ﴿ ولهو ﴾ كلهو الفتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain-grown plants flourish, then wither and become debris; the world's brief beauty and little lasting benefit are like such vegetation.
rows.anchor: شبه حال الدنيا وسرعة تقضيها مع قدلة جدواها بنبات أنبته الغيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “disbelievers” delighted by the plants may be literal deniers of God's favor or, by another reading, farmers.
rows.anchor: الجاحدون لنعمة الله فيما رزقهم من الغيث والنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plants' ruin is a punishment for ingratitude, as happened to the garden owners and the owner of the two gardens.
rows.anchor: فبعث عليه العاهة فهاج واصفر وصار حطاما عقوبة لهم على جحودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife holds severe punishment for unbelievers and forgiveness and approval from God for believers; these are grave realities unlike worldly amusements.
rows.anchor: يعني أن الدنيا وما فيها ليست إلا من محقرات الأمور وهي اللعب واللهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative kāf phrase is a predicate: worldly life is like rain-grown vegetation; it is deceptive when relied upon.
rows.anchor: والكاف في كمثل غيث في محل رفع على أنه خبر بعد خبر أي الحياة الدنيا مثل غيث

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhū al-Nūn advises seekers not to seek or love the world: provisions come from it, but the place of rest is elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قال ذو النون يا معشر المريدين لا تطلبوا الدنيا وإن طلبتموها فلا تحبوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since this life is small and the next great, people should hasten toward forgiveness from punishment and entrance into Paradise.
rows.anchor: ولما حقر الدنيا وصغر أمرها وعظم أمر الآخرة بعث عباده عى الممارعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should fear God by obeying His commands and not opposing them.
rows.anchor: في أوامره فلا تخالفوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “a soul” narrows the number who examine what they sent ahead for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: نكر النفس تقليلا للأنفس النواظر فيما قد من للآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tomorrow” means Judgment Day, bringing it near, or figures the afterlife as tomorrow after the world's today; its indefinite form magnifies its unknown greatness.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة سماه باليوم الذي يلي يومك تقريبا له أو عبر عن الآخرة

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār reports words written at Paradise's gate: what was done was profit, what was sent ahead was gained, and what was left behind was loss.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك ابن دينار مكتوب على باب الجنة وجدناه ما عملنا ربحنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to fear God emphasizes it: the first concerns duties and the second avoiding sins; awareness of God's scrutiny encourages vigilance.
rows.anchor: كرر الامر بالتقوى تأكيدا واتقوا الله أداء الواجبات لأنه قرن بما هو عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children should not distract from the five prayers or Qur'an; their management, increase, affection, and care can occupy people.
rows.anchor: لا تشغلكم ﴿ أموالكم ﴾ والتصرف فيها والسعي في تدبير امرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to become busy investing wealth instead of managing one's afterlife, or pleasing children instead of preparing for return to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل من يشتغل بثمير أمواله عن تدبير أحواله وبمرضاة أولاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such people lose their trade by selling the enduring for the transient.
rows.anchor: في تجارتهم حيث باعوا الباقي بالفاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The required spending is obligatory charity from part of God's provision, before death's signs make further delay impossible.
rows.anchor: من للتبعيض والمرد بالانفاق الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may address believers or hypocrites; the request is for a short reprieve to give charity and become righteous believers.
rows.anchor: من المؤمنين والآية في المؤمنين وقيل في المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads “and I become” with accusative, coordinated to the preceding form; jussive connects it to the conditional meaning “if You delay me, I will give.”
rows.anchor: وأكون أبو عمرو بالنصب عطفا على اللفظ والجزم على موضع فأصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul's appointed death, written in the Preserved Tablet, will be postponed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذا جاء أجلها ﴾ المكتوب في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “they do” instead of “you do”; knowing that death cannot be delayed and deeds will be requited should prompt people to fulfill obligations and prepare to meet God.
rows.anchor: يعملون حماد ويحيى المعنى أنكم اذا علمتم أن تأخير الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day” is governed by “you will be informed,” or invites the listener to remember the day everyone is gathered.
rows.anchor: يوم يجمع فيه الأولون والآخرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual loss is like losing a trade: the blessed occupy places the damned would have had, and the damned lose places they might have had; this is true loss, unlike worldly loss.
rows.anchor: وهو مستعار من تغابن القوم في التجارة وهو أن يغبن بعضهم بعضا لنزول السعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever believes and does good” describes a source of action; the Medinan and Syrian readings use first-person plural for “We erase” and “We admit.”
rows.anchor: صفة للمصدر أي عملا صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every affluent or constrained person should spend according to his means; this concerns provision for divorced women and nursing mothers.
rows.anchor: أي لينفق كل واحد من الموسر والمعسر ما بلغه وسعه يريد ما أمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A constrained provision is a narrow amount allotted by God in proportion to one's capacity; God does not require beyond the provision He gave.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قدر عليه رزقه ضيق أي رزقه الله على قدر قوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises ease after hardship to the person in straitened circumstances.
rows.anchor: بعد ضيق في المعيشة سعة وهذا وعد لذي العسر باليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested Mecca's people with famine and hunger after the Prophet prayed that Mudar suffer hardship like Joseph's years.
rows.anchor: امتحنا أهل مكة بالقحط والجوع حتى أكلوا الجيف والرمم بدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden belonged to people of Ṣarwān near Ḍarwān outside Ṣanʿāʾ; their father took his family's food and gave the rest to the poor.
rows.anchor: هم قوم من أهل الصلات كانت لأبيهم هذه الجنة بقربة يقال لها ضرو أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their father died, the sons feared poverty and resolved to harvest secretly at dawn before the poor appeared; they did not make an exception.
rows.anchor: فلما مات قال بنوه أن فعلنا ما كان يفعل أبونا ضاق علينا الامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the owners were unbelievers, while the majority holds they were otherwise; the blight destroyed their orchard.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن كانوا كفارا والجمهور على الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not say “if God wills”; this is called an exception although formally it is a condition, since both expressions mean that the act occurs only if God wills.
rows.anchor: ولا يقولون إن شاء الله وسمى استثناء وإن كان شرطا صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A calamity from God came upon the orchard while its owners slept; one report says God sent a fire that burned it.
rows.anchor: نزل عليها بلاء قيل أنزل الله تعالى عليها نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden became like dark night because it burned black, or like dawn as a treeless white plain, or like a cut-off orchard deprived of fruit.
rows.anchor: كالليل المظلم أي احترقت فاسودت أو كالصبح أي صارت أرضا بيضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At morning, some called out to the others.
rows.anchor: نادى بعضم بعضا عند الصباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Go early upon your harvest” uses “upon” because they approached to reap, or because go is given the sense of approaching; they intended to cut the crop.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل إلى حرثكم لأن الغدو اليه ليصرموه كان غدوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They went off whispering to one another so the poor would not hear.
rows.anchor: يتسارون فيما بينهم لئلا يسمع المساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle “an” may explain their whispering; if omitted, a verb of saying is understood. They prohibit enabling a poor person to enter, not merely his entering.
rows.anchor: وان مفسرة وقرئ بطرحها باضمار القول أي يتخافتون يقولون لا يدخلنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥard may mean determination to prevent the poor, or direction and speed; it may also name the orchard itself.
rows.anchor: على جد في المنع ﴿ قادرين ﴾ عند أنفسهم على المنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On first seeing the burned garden, they thought they had gone astray and reached the wrong place; after looking carefully, they recognized it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قالوا ﴾ في بديهة وصولهم ﴿ إنا لضالون ﴾ أي ضللنا جنتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They then realized their deprivation was the result of their own wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: حرمنا خيرها لجنايتنا على أنفسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle brother was the most upright and best among them.
rows.anchor: أعدلهم وخيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Why did you not glorify God?” can mean say “if God wills,” since both expressions magnify God, or remember Him and repent of their malicious plan.
rows.anchor: هلا تستثنون إذ الاستثناء التسبيح لالتقائهما في معنى التعظيم لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle brother had earlier urged them to remember God's punishment and repent, but they disobeyed, so he rebuked them.
rows.anchor: كان أوسطهم قال لهم حين عزموا على ذلك اذكروا الله وانتقامه من المجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the orchard was ruined, they finally said what they had been urged to say beforehand, admitted injustice in withholding charity and failing to make an exception, and declared God free of injustice.
rows.anchor: فتكلموا بعد خراب البصرة بما كان يدعوهم إلى التكلم به أولا وأقروا على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” denotes the species, allowing worshippers to be excepted; Ibn ʿAbbās explains halūʿ by the next two verses as quickly distressed at harm and withholding at good.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما تفسيره ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Halūʿ is quick distress when touched by harm and quick withholding when touched by good; one who receives good hoards it and denies it to others.
rows.anchor: والهلع سرعة الجزع عند مس المكروه لسرعة المنع عند مس الخير

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر
rows.claim: When asked by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir, Thaʿlab replied that God's own explanation is clearest.
rows.anchor: وسأل محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر ثعلبا عن الهلع فقال قد فسره الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is human temperament, but people are commanded to oppose their temperament and follow revealed law; harm may be poverty or illness and good may be wealth or health.
rows.anchor: وهذا طبعه وهو مأمور بمخالفة طبعه وموافقة شرعه والشر الضر والفقر والخير السعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can shield the Prophet from God's punishment if he disobeys; Salih said similarly, “Who would help me against God if I disobeyed Him?” There is no refuge besides God.
rows.anchor: كقول صالح عليه السلام فمن ينصرني من الله ان عصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choking food is what sticks in the throat and cannot be swallowed, identified as ḍarīʿ or zaqqūm; its pain reaches the heart.
rows.anchor: أي الذي ينشب في الحلوق فلا ينساغ يعني الضريع الزقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet recited the verse and fainted.
rows.anchor: وروى انه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأه هذه الآية فصعق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, while fasting, put aside his meal for three successive evenings when the verse came to mind; Thābit al-Bunānī and others eventually persuaded him to drink a sip of gruel.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه امسى صائما فأتى بطعام فعرضت له هذه الآية فقال ارفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings “adbara” (attributed to Nāfiʿ, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza, Yaʿqūb, and Khalaf) and “dabara” both mean the night departed; the latter may mean it came after daytime.
rows.anchor: نافع وحفص وحمزة ويعقوب وخلف وغيرهم أدبر ومعناهما ولى وذهب وقيل أدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfar means that dawn became bright; the oath's answer follows.
rows.anchor: اضاء وجواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It” is Hell, and al-kubar is the plural of kubrā: one of the calamities, unequalled in greatness.
rows.anchor: هي جمع الكبرى أي لإحدى البلايا أو الدواهي الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhīran is a specification of “one of the great calamities,” meaning a warning, and “for humankind” is an appositive.
rows.anchor: تمييز من إحدى أي أنها لإحدى الدواهي إنذارا كقولك وهي إحدى النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person will be told about the deeds he performed and what he left undone.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بما قدم ﴾ من عمل عمله ﴿ وأخر ﴾ ما لم يعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is Adam, who spent forty years as shaped clay before the spirit was breathed into him; his name and intended role were unknown.
rows.anchor: آدم عليه السلام ﴿ حين من الدهر ﴾ ر أربعون سنة مصورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A time passed over him” cannot describe nonexistence, and “not mentioned” is a circumstantial accusative describing the human as then unknown.
rows.anchor: ولو كان غير موجود لم يوصف بأنه قد أتى عليه حين من الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's name means prayer: morning is Fajr and early evening means Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واذكر اسم ربك ﴾ صل له ﴿ بكرة ﴾ صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muʿṣirāt may be clouds close to being squeezed by winds into rain, or the winds that form clouds and draw their moisture; a report says winds carry water from the sky to clouds.
rows.anchor: أي السحائب إذا أعصرت أي شارفت أن تعصرها الرياح فتمطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thajjājan means abundant, pouring water.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ماء ثجاجا ﴾ منصبا بكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water brings out grain, such as wheat and barley, and vegetation such as pasture.
rows.anchor: ﴿ حبا ﴾ كالبر والشعير ﴿ ونباتا ﴾ وكلأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alfāfan means gardens with densely intertwined trees; its singular may be laf, lafīf, absent, or the phrase may be a plural of a plural.
rows.anchor: ملتفة الأشجار واحدها لف كجذع وأجذاع ولفيف كشريف وأشراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no stopping from “Did We not make” through “thick gardens”; a necessary pause occurs at either “pegs” or “livelihood.”
rows.anchor: ولا وقف من ألم نجعل إلى ألفافا والوقف الضروري على أوتادا معاشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision separates benefactor from wrongdoer and truth from falsehood; it is a fixed endpoint for recompense or an appointed time for reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيا محدودا ومنتهى معلوما لوقوع الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Great Calamity overwhelms and surpasses all calamities; it may be the second trumpet blast or the Hour when people are driven to their final abodes.
rows.anchor: الداهية العظمى التى تطم على الدواهى أى تعلو وتغلب وهى النفخة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day” is in apposition to the coming calamity; people recall their deeds written in the record, though they had forgotten them. “What he strove for” may be a verbal noun or relative phrase.
rows.anchor: أعماله مدونة فى كتابه تذكرها وكان قد نسيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing one's Lord's standing means knowing that one will stand for judgment; the self is the commanding soul and desire is its harmful inclination.
rows.anchor: أى علم أن له مقاما يوم القيامة لحساب ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view describes someone about to commit a sin who remembers the coming judgment and abandons it; desire is the soul's attraction to its cravings.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو الرجل يهم بالمعصية فيذكر مقامه للحساب فيتركها والهوى ميل النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is the destination and place of return.
rows.anchor: أى المرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask when the Hour will be established, meaning when God will set it in place.
rows.anchor: متى ارساؤها أى اقامتها يعنى متى يقيمها الله تعالى ويثبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What are you in relation to its remembrance?” asks how he could tell or explain its time; the Prophet repeatedly mentioned it and asked about it, so the question expresses surprise at his concern.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يزل يذكر الساعة ويسأل عنها حتى نزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The endpoint of knowledge of the Hour's timing belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: منتهى علمها متى تكون لا يعلمها غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question is rejected because the Prophet's sending as the last prophet is itself a sign of the Hour; a pause after “in what” is possible before the independent statement about its endpoint.
rows.anchor: أى فيم هذا السؤال ثم قال أنت من ذكراها أى ارسالك وأنت آخر الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was sent to warn people who fear the Hour's terrors, not to tell them its time; Yazīd and ʿAbbās read nadhīrun with tanwīn.
rows.anchor: لم تبعث لتعلمهم بوقت الساعة وإنما بعثت لتنذر من أهوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Hour, people will think they stayed in this world only an evening or its noon, because the terror makes the duration seem short; this means less than a full day.
rows.anchor: استقلوا مدة لبثهم فى الدنيا لما عاينوا من الهول كقوله لم يلبثوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The noon of the evening” is licensed by the two periods' relation within one day: their stay did not reach an entire day, only one end of it.
rows.anchor: وإنما صحت اضافة الضحى إلى العشية للملابسة بينهما لاجتماعهما فى نهار واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person flees his brother, mother, and father because of claims owed between them or because he is occupied with himself.
rows.anchor: لتبعات بينه وبينهم أو لاشتغاله بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order starts with a brother, then parents as closer relatives, then spouse and children as especially beloved.
rows.anchor: بدأ بالأخ ثم بالأبوين لأنهما أقرب منه ثم بالصاحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report names Abel as the first to flee his brother, Abraham from his parents, Noah and Lot from their wives, and Noah from his son.
rows.anchor: قيل أول من يفر منأخيه هابيل ومن أبويه إبراهيم ومن صاحبته نوح ولوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsʿasa is a word with opposite senses: night may be arriving in darkness or departing.
rows.anchor: أقبل بظلامه أو أدبر فهو من الاضداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn's light extends; because dawn brings air and breeze, its arrival is figuratively called breathing. It is the oath's answer.
rows.anchor: امتد ضوءه ولما كان اقبال الصبح يلازمه الروح والنسيم جعل ذلك نفسا له مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by dawn, meaning morning, as in “the morning when it grows light,” or by the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالفجر وهو الصبح كقوله والصبح إذا أسفر أو بصلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The night” may mean the Night of Decree; yasri means it passes, though its final yāʾ is dropped in connected recitation and at pause.
rows.anchor: إذا يمضى وياء يسر تحذف فى الدرج اكتفاء عنها بالكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked why the yāʾ is absent, al-Akhfash first said the questioner must serve him a year, then explained that night does not travel but one travels within it; transferred usage permits “a sleeping night.”
rows.anchor: وسأل واحد الاخفش عن سقوط الياء فقال لا حتى تخدمنى سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijr means intellect, which restrains a person from improper conduct; the question asks whether the intelligent recognize the oath's greatness or its force in confirming the omitted threat of punishment.
rows.anchor: عقل سمى به لأنه يحجر عن النهافت فيما لا ينبغى كما سمى عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of the oath is that the deniers will be punished, indicated by the later question and account of punishment.
rows.anchor: والمقسم عليه محذوف وهو قوله ليعذبن يدل عليه قوله ألم تر إلى قوله فصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell may be brought forth visibly, as in the verse about it being exposed to the straying, or literally brought on the Day; a report describes seventy thousand reins, each drawn by seventy thousand angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو مجرى على حقيقة ففى الحديث يؤتى بجهنم يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person will take heed then, but the remembrance can no longer benefit him.
rows.anchor: ومن أين له منفعة الذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wishes he had sent righteous deeds ahead during fleeting life for the enduring life of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: هذه وهى حياة الآخرة أى ياليتنى قدمت الأعمال الصالحة فى الحياة الفانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings endure the hardships and calamities of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: مشقة يكابد مصائب الدنيا وشدائد الآخرة

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhū al-Nūn says a person remains bound by divine decree and summoned to obey and refrain.
rows.anchor: وعن ذى النون لم يزل مربوطا بحبل القضاء مدعوا إلى الائتمار والانتهاء
